title: legacy chat intermediary for streamed tool invocations and structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Many Redwood customers use existing SDKs and proxies that expect OpenAI Chat Completions (chat.completions) semantics. We must offer a compatibility intermediary that maps incoming OpenAI-style requests into Redwood's canonical API and maps outbound streamed events back into the Chat Completions streamed event framing. This ticket covers the hardest part: preserving fidelity for interleaved streamed tool/function-calling invocations and structured JSON outputs while guaranteeing idempotency and clear failure semantics.

Scope and goals:
- Accept OpenAI Chat Completions request payloads (messages, functions, function_call hints) and translate to Redwood API calls without requiring client changes.
- Stream responses back in an OpenAI-compatible event envelope (data: {...}) for both partial content and tool call events.
- Handle tool/function calls that may start during streaming, return partial arguments across multiple delta frames, and then produce a final tool_result event. Map this to Redwood's function call model while ensuring the client sees expected oa-cc frames.
- Enforce structured output contracts (e.g., top-level JSON with schema hints) and surface schema validation failures as metadata compatible with OpenAI clients.
- Provide robust telemetry: token attribution, event latency (first byte, tool call start/end), and error codes for compatibility mapping failures.

Non-goals:
- Reimplement full OpenAI API; only the chat.completions subset required for our customers.
- Long-term protocol divergence features (those belong to a future v2 gateway).

Key decision areas:
1) Event framing: We'll use the oa-cc SSE "data: [STREAM]" envelope for streaming, with a special compatibility field "x-redwood-compat-version" to allow graceful evolution.
2) Tool-call assembly: We will buffer delta frames for function arguments on the intermediary and publish a synthesized "tool_call_started" SSE event on first detection, incremental "tool_call_arg_delta" events for deltas, and a final "tool_call_result" event. This avoids exposing Redwood internal RPCs to clients.
3) Idempotency & replay: Each incoming request will be assigned a compatibility-level request_id; retries must be idempotent. We'll include a "compatempotency_token" computed from the OpenAI request id or generated server-side.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests demonstrating streamed generation with a 3-part function argument (deltas across three chunks) map to three oa-cc SSE deltas and one final tool call completion event.
- Existing Redwood customers using an OpenAI-compatible SDK can switch the endpoint to the intermediary with no client changes and observe identical message ordering for both normal and tool-invocation flows.
- Telemetry dashboards show event latencies and a compatibility-mapping error rate < 0.1% in staging.
- Unit tests for schema enforcement, including injected malformed JSON and partial EOF mid-JSON in a delta chunk.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (spike): Build a prototype intermediary in the compatibility service that accepts oa-cc requests and emits canonical Redwood calls, focusing on streaming frames assembly (2 weeks). Outcome: prototype server and test harness.
- Phase 2 (engine): Implement buffering behavior for function argument deltas, deterministic synthesis of tool_call_started/arg_delta/result SSE events, and compatempotency handling (3 weeks).
- Phase 3 (tests & telemetry): Create end-to-end tests with simulated clients, integrate telemetry tags, and add dashboards (1 week).
- Phase 4 (canary rollout): Canary in staging >72 hours, monitor error/latency, then gradual rollout to low-traffic prod routes (2 weeks).

Implementation details and trade-offs:
- We chose to buffer argument deltas server-side (vs. streaming raw deltas through) to ensure we can validate JSON against expected shapes before emitting final tool_call_result. This introduces small additional memory usage per open stream but simplifies error semantics for clients.
- For streaming performance we will keep delta buffering incremental and emit arg_delta SSEs to clients as soon as each chunk arrives; the buffer is only for validation and final assembly.
- To avoid breaking clients that expect specific SSE sequences, we preserve existing oa-cc field names and only add namespaced Redwood fields under "redwood_compat".

Test plan:
- Unit: function-call assembly, schema validation failures, partial chunk EOF, backpressure behavior (slow client), and idempotency token collisions.
- Integration: end-to-end with JS SDK, Python SDK, and a lightweight proxy that replays captured real production request traces.
- Load test: concurrent 2k streaming connections with average 3 function-invocations per request; measure 95th percentile latency and memory usage.

Telemetry & observability:
- New trace tags: "compat.request_id", "compat.request_size_bytes", "compat.tool_calls", "compat.stream_first_byte_ms".
- Metrics: compatibility_map_errors_total, compat_latency_first_byte_histogram, compat_tool_assembly_duration_ms.
- Dashboards: compat health, tool-call error breakdown by schema failure vs. missing function definition.

Rollout and rollback:
- Canary: deploy to staging and a single low-traffic prod region with feature-flag gating.
- Rollback criteria: >1% mapping error rate, or latency regressions >20% on p95 for any monitored route.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Some clients generate malformed incremental JSON (e.g., emit trailing commas or partial multibyte UTF-8 boundaries). Mitigation: robust incremental parser that tolerates partial UTF-8 and emits a clear compatibility error frame rather than silently dropping tokens.
- Risk: Memory pressure with many long-lived streams. Mitigation: per-request soft limits and circuit-breaker with clear 4xx style compatibility responses.

Deliverables:
- Compatibility intermediary implementation and tests.
- SDK examples in JS/Python demonstrating no client change required.
- Telemetry dashboards and alerting rules.

comments: 2025-02-14 - Liam Chen: Spiked a prototype that re-emits SSE frames. Observed edge case when function arg chunk boundary splits a multi-byte emoji; implemented partial UTF-8 buffering fix.
2025-02-20 - PM (Sofia Martinez): Please ensure the UX for schema validation failures surfaces both a human-friendly message and a machine-readable code so clients can programmatically fallback.

2025-02-25 - Design review (Marco Ruiz): OK with synthesized 'tool_call_started' and 'tool_call_arg_delta' events, but prefer 'redwood_compat.version' in SSE meta vs x- header. Updated plan accordingly.
2025-02-28 - Security (Priya Nair): Confirmed compat endpoint must log minimal PII and redact user-provided function arg payloads when flagged. Added telemetry redaction checklist.
